name: Abstinences, Illimitables & Wisdom
intro: The last six beautiful factors arise only in particular moments: three abstinences from the Eightfold Path, two illimitables you know from the brahmavihāras, and the faculty of wisdom that completes the fifty-two.

words.gloss: right speech; abstaining from wrong speech

etymology.note: as a cetasika it is the moment of refraining — the lie not told, the harsh word held back

words.gloss: right action; abstaining from wrong bodily conduct

etymology.note: the refraining from killing, taking, and sexual wrongdoing, in the moment of the choice

words.gloss: right livelihood; abstaining from wrong ways of earning a living

etymology.root: sammā (rightly) + ājīva (livelihood, from ā + √jīv, to live)
etymology.note: the same refraining, when the wrong speech or act would have been for one's living

words.gloss: faculty of wisdom; non-delusion as a controlling power

etymology.note: amoha on the chart — the factor that sees anicca, dukkha, anattā; the direct opposite of moha

talk.text: The nineteen common beautiful factors are always there; these six come when called. When a wrong word is about to leave and doesn't, that is
; when it would have been for your living,
. When the heart opens toward suffering it is
— the two illimitables that are factors in their own right, where
were adosa and tatramajjhattatā under other names. And
as a faculty — the seeing that undoes
. Fifty-two factors, and the chart is complete.

suttaRec.title: Vibhaṅga — Analysis of the Path
suttaRec.blurb: The Buddha defines each factor of the Eightfold Path in turn — right speech, action, and livelihood as the three abstinences.
